Legacy campaign

The Power You Don't Build (1962–1981)

The oil shocks are coming. Help homes and businesses use less electricity, and find out what that saves your utility.

Explore the Legacy campaign↗ See what’s at stake ↓

Build one utility across nine generations. This chapter is part of that journey.

Location
A fictional California utility
Starts in
1962
Generation
20 years

The situation

Your starting point

Your fifth Legacy term runs through the oil-price shocks of the 1970s. How exposed the company is depends on the fleet handed down by earlier generations.

The featured goal asks for electricity savings from efficiency in homes and businesses. Meeting demand can mean building more supply, but it can also mean reducing the amount customers need to use. Both choices have costs and timing to consider.

The choices

What will you do?

  1. 01

    Compare savings with new supply

    Look at efficiency alongside generation projects. Electricity saved can reduce the fuel and capacity needed to serve the same customers.

  2. 02

    Prepare for expensive oil

    Review the inherited fleet's fuel exposure before the shocks arrive. Decisions made in the quieter years shape the bills that follow.

  3. 03

    Meet the term's goals together

    Track efficiency savings alongside customer retention, affordability and debt. A successful policy still has to fit the utility's finances.

Put your plan to the test

Try meeting more of your customers' needs with less electricity to generate.

Open the campaign setup to begin, or continue your existing company. Later generations inherit the choices you made before them.
